ZinStd.Principles: Written in Zin after bootstrap; no required libc; explicit allocators; target-specific OS code isolated under std.os; protocol/data-format functionality is implemented as ordinary Zin modules rather than compiler special cases.
ZinStd.Modules: std.mem std.heap std.fmt std.io std.fs std.math std.meta std.atomic std.Thread std.time std.process std.testing std.posix std.os std.json std.xml std.wayland

DataModules.Module: JSON parser/encoder implemented in Zin and able to specialize through comptime reflection.
XML tokenizer/parser/DOM or pull-parser primitives implemented in Zin. It is used by stdlib bootstrap tooling such as Wayland protocol materialization.

ZinStd.Wayland: std.wayland is constructed from canonical Wayland XML during the standard-library bootstrap and thereafter imported normally. Users do not register schemas or protocols in build.zin.
ZinStd.Freestanding: Core language and freestanding programs do not require std.
